newsitem.title: USA: Dayton May same-store sales up 4.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dayton May same-store sales up 4.3 pct.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said same-store sales increased 4.3 percent for the four weeks ended May 31.
Net retail sales for the month rose 9.8 percent to $1.891 billion from $1.722 billion a year ago.
"Sales in May were on plan at Target and Mervyn's, and slightly below plan at the Department Store Division," said chief executive Bob Ulrich.
Dayton said that May and year-to-date sales by operating division were as follows:

-- Target's total sales for the month increased 14.3 percent and comparable-store sales increased 5.5 percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales increased 13.9 percent and comparable-store sales increased 5.2 percent.

-- Mervyn's total sales for the month decreased 3.2 percent while comparable-store sales increased 2.7 percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales decreased 3.9 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 1.1 percent.

-- The Department Store division's total sales for the month increased 1.3 percent while comparable-store sales decreased 0.9 percent. Year-to-date, the Department Stores' total sales were even with last year and comparable-store sales decreased 2.8 percent, Dayton said.

Total company sales for the 17 weeks ended May 31 were $7.627 billion, up 9.1 percent from $6.991 billion in the same period a year ago. Same-store sales for the 17-week period were up 3.2 percent compared with the same period last year.
Dayton Hudson operates 1,092 stores in 39 states, including 752 Target stores, 276 Mervyn's stores and 64 department stores.
